payload.task_text:
You are a research assistant preparing a literature review on transformer architectures in natural language processing. Your goal is to collect papers from multiple academic sources, analyze them, organize them in a knowledge base, and produce a comprehensive review document.

Start by searching the scholarly database for papers related to "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers related to "attention mechanism" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Query the scholarly paper catalog through the scholarly MCP — its search-arxiv tool returns arXiv-style entries that include paper IDs, which you will need for the overlap analysis below. Retrieve all available papers and note their titles, authors, publication years, and journal references.

Next, search the arxiv repository (via the arxiv_local MCP) for papers about "transformer", then run a second, separate search for papers about "neural network" — two searches, one per phrase — and combine (union) the results, removing duplicates. Download and read through the abstracts of the papers you find to understand what each paper covers.

Write and run a Python analysis script. The script should take the collected paper data and categorize each paper into one of these methodology categories: "Architecture Design" for papers proposing new model architectures, "Training Methods" for papers about training techniques or optimization, "Applications" for papers applying transformers to specific tasks, and "Survey" for papers that review or survey the field. Assign categories based on keywords in the title and abstract. The script should also identify which papers appear in both databases (overlap analysis by matching paper IDs).

Create a database in the knowledge base titled "Research Paper Tracker" with properties for Title (title type), Paper_ID (rich_text), Authors (rich_text), Year (number), Category (select with options Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey), Source (select with options Scholarly, Arxiv, Both), and Abstract_Summary (rich_text). Add a page entry for each unique paper found across both databases.

Create a Word document called Transformer_Literature_Review.docx in the workspace. The document should have a title "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP", followed by an introduction section explaining the scope of the review. Then include a section for each methodology category listing the papers in that category with their titles, authors, year, and a brief description from the abstract. End with a conclusion section summarizing the state of the field and identifying research gaps.

Create an Excel file called Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx in the workspace with three sheets. The first sheet "Paper_Catalog" should have columns Paper_ID, Title, Authors, Year, Source (Scholarly, Arxiv, or Both), and Category. The second sheet "Method_Comparison" should have columns Category, Paper_Count, Avg_Year, and Key_Papers (listing titles of papers in that category). The third sheet "Citation_Matrix" should list all unique papers with columns Paper_ID, Title, In_Scholarly (Yes or No), In_Arxiv (Yes or No), and Overlap (Yes if in both, No otherwise). Write paper IDs as plain text (e.g. 1706.03762) and all other cell values as literal values — do not write Excel formulas.

Your workspace contains review_guidelines.json with category definitions and lit_review_template.md with formatting guidance.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, use two dependency waves. The main agent first dynamically locates and reads review_guidelines.json and lit_review_template.md from the task-visible workspace.

Wave 1 — dispatch exactly two source sub-agents in parallel:
1. explore 0 (academic-literature-researcher 0): One explore sub-agent calls the Scholarly search-arxiv tool exactly twice, once for transformer and once for attention mechanism. It returns the complete responses available from those two calls, normalized arXiv-style paper IDs, titles, authors, years, journal references, abstracts, query membership, duplicate IDs, and missing-field controls. It is strictly read-only.
2. explore 1 (academic-literature-researcher 1): One explore sub-agent owns the local-arXiv branch. It calls search_papers exactly twice for transformer and neural network with the service's largest safe result limit, deduplicates normalized IDs, then uses download_paper and read_paper for each unique result as needed to verify its abstract. It writes no final artifact; if the corpus is large, it persists one runtime-unique JSON in the discovered task workspace and returns only path/hash/counts plus compact metadata controls.

After Wave 1, the main agent reconciles IDs without losing source membership, then writes and runs the required Python analysis script. The script consumes the two verified corpora, unions by normalized Paper_ID, labels Source as Scholarly/Arxiv/Both, assigns exactly one of Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey from the guidelines and title/abstract evidence, and emits one canonical runtime JSON containing all unique papers, overlap flags, category counts, and controls. Read the script and JSON back before Wave 2.

Wave 2 — dispatch exactly three coder sub-agents in parallel from that same canonical JSON:
1. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the exact-title Notion database Research Paper Tracker. Fully paginate search before create/reuse, block on duplicate exact-title databases/pages, enforce Title, Paper_ID, Authors, Year, Category, Source, Abstract_Summary with exact types/options, upsert one page per Paper_ID, and query/read all managed pages back.
2. coder 1 (office-report-builder 0): Sole writer of Transformer_Literature_Review.docx. Follow lit_review_template.md, use the exact title and category sections, cover every unique paper with abstract-grounded text, add evidence-based gaps, and read the document back.
3. coder 2 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx. Create exactly Paper_Catalog, Method_Comparison, Citation_Matrix; use plain-text IDs and literal values, preserve every source flag/category, and read all populated ranges back.

Each writer must self-correct before returning. The main agent compares only IDs, counts, categories, titles, years and overlap flags across the three receipts; no third wave or repair agent is allowed.

nodes.text:
I am building a literature review on transformer architectures in NLP. I have already searched and downloaded 9 arXiv papers using the arxiv_local MCP. Your job is to READ each downloaded paper and report back a concise structured summary of each.

Read each paper with the tool `mcp__arxiv_local__read_paper`, passing the paper ID as `paper_id`. The 9 paper IDs are:
1. 1706.03762
2. 2009.06732
3. 1810.04805
4. 2005.14165
5. 1910.10683
6. 1409.0473
7. 1207.00580
8. 1502.03167
9. 1312.06199

For EACH paper, report back the following fields:
- Paper_ID (the arXiv ID as given above)
- Title (exact)
- Authors (full list of author names as given in the paper)
- Year (publication year)
- Abstract (the abstract text — quote it verbatim if available; if the paper only has a short summary, give that)
- Key focus: 1-2 sentences describing what the paper actually covers (method/architecture, training technique, application to a task, or survey/review)
- Venue/Journal reference: any journal, conference, or venue reference mentioned in the paper (e.g., NeurIPS 2017, ACM Computing Surveys). If none is mentioned, say "none mentioned".

Constraints:
- This is a read-only task: do not download anything new, do not create or modify any files.
- Do not search for additional papers; only read the 9 listed.
- Keep your final report compact and structured (one block per paper). Do not paste entire paper bodies back to me — just the fields above.

Deliverable: a structured report with all 9 papers, each with the fields listed above.
Read 9 arXiv papers

Create an Excel workbook for a literature review on transformer architectures in NLP. You are producing one deliverable file.

CONTEXT
- Working directory (workspace): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace
- All paper data has already been collected and analyzed. Read the file `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/analysis_results.json`. It contains:
  - `papers`: list of 9 paper objects with keys paper_id, title, authors (comma-joined string), year, category, source ("Scholarly" | "Arxiv" | "Both"), in_scholarly (bool), in_arxiv (bool), overlap (bool), abstract, abstract_summary.
  - `method_comparison`: list of 4 objects with keys category, paper_count, avg_year, key_papers (semicolon-joined titles).
  - `citation_matrix`: list of 9 objects with keys paper_id, title, in_scholarly ("Yes"/"No"), in_arxiv ("Yes"/"No"), overlap ("Yes"/"No").
- Paper ID examples look like "1706.03762", "2009.06732" — arXiv-style IDs.

DELIVERABLE
Create the file: `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/Research_Paper_Analysis.xlsx`

It must contain exactly three sheets:

1. Sheet named "Paper_Catalog" with header row and columns (in this order):
   Paper_ID | Title | Authors | Year | Source | Category
   One row per paper (all 9, in the order they appear in `papers`). Source values must be exactly one of "Scholarly", "Arxiv", "Both". Category values must be exactly one of "Architecture Design", "Training Methods", "Applications", "Survey".

2. Sheet named "Method_Comparison" with header row and columns (in this order):
   Category | Paper_Count | Avg_Year | Key_Papers
   One row per methodology category — include all 4 categories (Architecture Design, Training Methods, Applications, Survey), even if a category has zero papers. Paper_Count is an integer; Avg_Year is the numeric average year (e.g. 2016.8; use an empty cell or 0 if the category has no papers); Key_Papers is the semicolon-joined list of titles from `key_papers`.

3. Sheet named "Citation_Matrix" with header row and columns (in this order):
   Paper_ID | Title | In_Scholarly | In_Arxiv | Overlap
   One row per unique paper (all 9). In_Scholarly / In_Arxiv / Overlap are literal text values "Yes" or "No" taken from `citation_matrix`.

HARD REQUIREMENTS
- Paper_ID values MUST be written as plain text strings (e.g. the literal text 1706.03762), never as numbers, never as Excel formulas, and never with a leading apostrophe trick that shows in the cell value. If the Excel MCP writes them as strings, that is correct. Verify after writing that the cells read back as text like "1706.03762".
- ALL cell values must be literal values. Do NOT write any Excel formula anywhere in the workbook (no =, no SUM, no AVERAGE). Compute Avg_Year yourself from the data already in analysis_results.json.
- Year should be an integer number; Avg_Year a number; everything else text.
- Include a bold header row on each sheet. Keep it clean and readable (you may set column widths / bold headers), but content correctness is what matters.

Suggested approach: use the `mcp__excel__create_workbook`, `mcp__excel__create_worksheet` / `mcp__excel__rename_worksheet`, and `mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel` tools, plus `mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel` to verify. You may also use `mcp__local__python_execute` (openpyxl is typically available) if that is more reliable — either way the final .xlsx must exist at the exact path above with the three sheets.

VERIFY before finishing: read back all three sheets and confirm (a) sheet names are exactly Paper_Catalog, Method_Comparison, Citation_Matrix; (b) row counts are 9, 4, and 9 data rows respectively; (c) no cell contains a formula; (d) paper IDs read back as text.

Report back: the exact file path, the three sheet names with their row counts, and confirmation that paper IDs are stored as text and no formulas exist.
Build Excel analysis workbook

Create a Word literature-review document on transformer architectures in NLP. You are producing one deliverable file.

CONTEXT
- Working directory (workspace): /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace
- All paper data has already been collected and analyzed. Read these two files:
  1. `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/analysis_results.json` — contains `papers` (9 objects: paper_id, title, authors, year, journal_ref, category, source ("Scholarly"|"Arxiv"|"Both"), abstract, abstract_summary), `method_comparison` (4 categories with paper_count, avg_year, key_papers), `citation_matrix`, and `stats` (unique_papers, in_both, arxiv_only, scholarly_only, earliest_year, latest_year, avg_year, category_counts).
  2. `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/lit_review_template.md` — formatting guidance (title, structure, min 500 words, group by category, highlight multi-database papers, include publication year trends).

BACKGROUND on how the papers were gathered (use this in the introduction): two searches were run on the scholarly paper catalogue ("transformer" and "attention mechanism") and two on the arXiv repository ("transformer" and "neural network"); each pair of results was unioned with duplicates removed by paper ID, giving 9 unique papers. 6 papers appear in BOTH databases, 3 appear only in arXiv. Papers span 2012-2020.

DELIVERABLE
Create: `/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/Transformer_Literature_Review.docx`

Required structure (use Word heading styles so the document has a real outline):
1. Document title, exactly: "Literature Review: Transformer Architectures in NLP" — as a top-level title/Heading 1.
2. "Introduction" section (Heading 1 or 2) explaining the scope of the review: the topic, the two databases searched and the four search phrases, the 9 unique papers found, the overlap (6 in both databases, 3 arXiv-only), the year range, and how papers were categorized into four methodology categories by keyword analysis of title and abstract.
3. One section per methodology category, in this order, each as its own heading: "Architecture Design", "Training Methods", "Applications", "Survey". Under each heading, include a 1-2 sentence description of what that category means, then list EVERY paper in that category. For each paper include: the paper title, the authors, the publication year, and a brief description drawn from its abstract (use `abstract_summary` or paraphrase `abstract`). A readable format is one paragraph per paper, e.g. "Attention Is All You Need (Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Niki Parmar, 2017). <brief description> ...". Also mention each paper's database source (Both / Arxiv) and clearly highlight which papers appear in both databases.
4. "Conclusion" section (Heading 1 or 2) summarizing the state of the field (e.g. the shift from recurrent/attention-augmented models to pure-attention architectures, then pre-training and scaling, then efficiency-focused work), publication-year trends observed in the corpus, and identifying research gaps (e.g. the corpus is small and English/NLP-centric; efficiency and long-context handling only represented by one survey; limited coverage of multilingual and low-resource NLP, interpretability, and domain-specific applications; three of the nine papers are general deep-learning rather than transformer-specific).

REQUIREMENTS
- Total document length: at least 500 words (aim for roughly 900-1300 words).
- Every one of the 9 papers must appear in the document, under its correct category section.
- Use real Word headings (not just bold text) so `get_document_outline` shows the structure.
- Do not fabricate papers, authors, years, or venues. Use only the data in analysis_results.json. Journal/venue refs are available in the `journal_ref` field for some papers if you want to mention them.
- Save the file at the exact path above.

Suggested tools: `mcp__word__create_document`, `mcp__word__add_heading`, `mcp__word__add_paragraph`, `mcp__word__add_page_break` (optional). Verify afterwards with `mcp__word__get_document_outline` and `mcp__word__get_document_info`, and confirm the file exists.

Report back: the exact file path, the document outline (headings), the approximate word count, and confirmation that all 9 papers appear with title/authors/year/description.
Build Word literature review

Add page entries to an existing Notion database. This is a write task using the Notion MCP tools.

CONTEXT
- A Notion database named "Research Paper Tracker" already exists with ID: 801c7f40-0136-470f-a080-f83e5db2ca7d
- Its properties are: Title (title), Paper_ID (rich_text), Authors (rich_text), Year (number), Category (select: Architecture Design / Training Methods / Applications / Survey), Source (select: Scholarly / Arxiv / Both), Abstract_Summary (rich_text).
- The data for the 9 papers is in this local file: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_glm-5.3/SingleUserTurn-terminal-arxiv-scholarly-notion-word-excel/workspace/analysis_results.json (read it with a filesystem read tool). Use the `papers` array; each element has paper_id, title, authors, year, category, source, abstract_summary.

TASK
Create ONE page (row) in that database for EACH of the 9 papers, using `mcp__notion__API-post-page` with:
- parent: {"type": "database_id", "database_id": "801c7f40-0136-470f-a080-f83e5db2ca7d"}
- properties (Notion property-value format):
  - "Title": {"title": [{"text": {"content": "<paper title>"}}]}
  - "Paper_ID": {"rich_text": [{"text": {"content": "<paper_id e.g. 1706.03762>"}}]}
  - "Authors": {"rich_text": [{"text": {"content": "<authors string>"}}]}
  - "Year": {"number": <year as integer>}
  - "Category": {"select": {"name": "<category>"}}
  - "Source": {"select": {"name": "<source: Scholarly | Arxiv | Both>"}}
  - "Abstract_Summary": {"rich_text": [{"text": {"content": "<abstract_summary>"}}]}

IMPORTANT — TOOL BEHAVIOR NOTE
I (the main agent) attempted `mcp__notion__API-post-page` myself and it repeatedly failed argument validation with an error like:
  Invalid args for tool "mcp__notion__API-post-page": /parent must be object; /parent must be object; /parent must be object; /parent must match exactly one schema in oneOf; /properties must be object
The same happened for `mcp__notion__API-patch-page` ("/properties must be object"). Other Notion tools (create-a-database, patch-block-children, post-search, retrieve-a-database, update-a-database) work fine for me.

So: try `mcp__notion__API-post-page` for the FIRST paper only. 
- If it succeeds, continue and create all 9 pages, then verify with `mcp__notion__API-post-database-query` on the database ID and report how many rows came back.
- If it fails with a validation error, try at most 2 alternative argument formats (e.g. parent as {"database_id": "..."} without a "type" key). If it still fails, STOP — do not spam retries, and do NOT try to fake the pages by other means. Report the exact error text you received and how many attempts you made.

CONSTRAINTS
- Do not create, rename, or modify any Notion database. Do not archive or delete anything.
- Do not touch any files in the workspace (reading analysis_results.json is allowed and required).
- Do not send email or interact with any other external system.

REPORT BACK: whether page creation succeeded or failed; if failed, the exact error message(s) and number of attempts; if succeeded, the list of page titles created and the row count returned by a database query.
Create Notion paper pages
